units.translation: But when the all-daring woman raised the cry
He changed his mind about the all-daring thought
More probable is πάντων τροφὸν [nourisher of all], which Lobeck conjectured.
the all-nourishing lake of the Ethiopians

which the scholiast explains as πάντοθεν συνηγμένα [gathered from all sides]: hence Meineke in Philologus vol. 19 p. 225 conjectured παντόσυρτα [swept together from all sides]. πάμφυρτος [all-mixed] was used by later writers indicated in the Thesaurus vol. 6 p. 121.
the many things mixed from all sources

which is similar to the Homeric τρήρωνα πέλειαν [timid dove] and agrees with the verb ὐπερδέδοικεν [fears exceedingly]. Therefore this seems to be the true reading, not πάντροφος [all-nourishing], which is noted in the Medicean manuscript, read by Tzetzes on Lycophron 87 and Eustathius p. 1602, 7, following the foolish interpretation of the scholiast: πάντροφον δὲ τὴν πελειάδα φησὶν, ὅτι πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα ἅπαξ τοῦ ἔτους τίκτει, ἡ δὲ περιστερὰ ἀεί · διὸ ἀνάκειται τῇ Ἀφροδίτη [he says the dove is all-nourishing because all birds lay eggs once a year, but the dove always; therefore it is dedicated to Aphrodite]. The Byzantine scholiasts repeated this with some changes.
as a dove, trembling at everything, fears exceedingly for its young, the serpents that share its bed
he says the dove is all-nourishing because all birds lay eggs once a year, but the dove always; therefore it is dedicated to Aphrodite
of the race turned in utter flight
corrupt for πᾶν τέλος ὃς νέμεις [you who dispense every fulfillment], as I said under παντελής [all-fulfilling].
In every way I must endure this boldness
For in no way will you persuade him
He has come in every way to announce something new
In no way will he put me to death
especially and in every way, and by the sisters of my father
especially and in every way, the gods below are better at taking than at letting go
especially and in every way, and when he happens to be in need
and you will make the land and city just in every way, passing your lives
πάνυ ταρφύς τις [a very frequent one] Franzius
For utterly a countless host of men has perished
one woman destroying many, very many souls under Troy
they are about to utterly bring destruction upon the house of Agamemnon forever
[πανωλέθροισιν ἐμβολαῖς [with utterly destructive attacks] introduced by an interpolator for ὁμοπτέροισιν ἐμβολαῖς [with attacks of like wings], about which I spoke under ὁμόπτερος [of like wings].]
Do not utterly destroy my city from its roots
of the same seed indeed and utterly destroyed
he mowed down the utterly destroyed native paternal house
the eye of the house, not to fall utterly destroyed
utterly destroyed he could never be
or may they perish utterly destroyed and most miserably
and he hurls mortals utterly destroyed from their high-towering hopes
